title: Bayesian diffusivity-spectrum estimation for prostate multi-b diffusion MRI

creators.name: Wells, William M., III
creators.affiliation: Department of Radiology, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA; Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA

creators.name: Maier, Stephan E.
creators.affiliation: Department of Radiology, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA

description:
Code, configuration, and cached posteriors accompanying the manuscript "Why ADC works: Bayesian spectral decomposition of prostate multi-b diffusion MRI" by Patrick Remerscheid, William M. Wells III and Stephan E. Maier, submitted to Magnetic Resonance in Medicine (2026).

Multi-b diffusion MRI signal decays from 149 prostate regions of interest (56 patients) are decomposed into an eight-component diffusivity spectrum, both by constrained-ridge maximum a posteriori estimation and by full Bayesian No-U-Turn Sampler inference that additionally infers the per-region noise level. The posterior establishes which diffusivity compartments an extended-b acquisition can actually resolve, and shows that tumour-versus-normal variation collapses onto a single restricted-to-free-water axis — which is why the scalar apparent diffusion coefficient is already a near-optimal spectral discriminant for region-of-interest lesion detection.

Verified from a clean clone: uv sync followed by uv run python -m spectra_estimation_dmri.biomarkers.recompute reproduces every number reported in the manuscript byte-identically. Per-figure scripts are documented in scripts/README.md.

The region-of-interest signal decays and tissue and Gleason-grade labels are deposited separately at 10.5281/zenodo.20787155.
notes: The manuscript results were produced at commit d34e203763e04768ebbde3ceb032564d8dc0350b (release v1.0.0). Later releases differ from that revision only in deposit metadata and documentation.
